findings.title: record_stored_segments() called on flusher-internal buffers instead of the main processing buffer
findings.body: In the old code, `self.buffer` was the same `SpansBuffer` instance used by `process_batch` to store spans via `buffer.process_spans(...)`. Now, the original `buffer` parameter passed to `SpanFlusher.__init__` is only used to read `assigned_shards` and is never stored. Instead, `self.buffers` contains new `SpansBuffer` instances created for flushing only. Calling `record_stored_segments()` on these flusher buffers is incorrect because they never store segments — the main buffer (shared with `process_batch`) does. This likely means the metric/recording that `record_stored_segments` provides is silently broken.

findings.title: Killed processes are never joined, creating zombie processes
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is detected as unhealthy, `process.kill()` is called but `process.join()` is never called to reap it. On Unix, this leaves a zombie process entry in the process table. If flusher processes crash repeatedly (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS=10 times per process index), zombie processes accumulate. Adding a `process.join(timeout=0)` or similar after `kill()` would reap the child.

findings.title: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard method is never called
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard` (singular shard) is defined at line 127 but is never invoked anywhere in the codebase. All call sites use `_create_process_for_shards` (plural). This is dead code that should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: join() may skip terminating remaining processes when deadline expires
findings.body: In `join()`, if `remaining_time <= 0` the code `break`s out of the entire for-loop, skipping `process.terminate()` for the current process and all subsequent processes. This means if `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes most of the timeout budget, some flusher processes may not receive `terminate()`. While daemon processes are eventually killed on interpreter exit, during graceful shutdown (e.g., in a long-running consumer), these processes could continue producing to Kafka after the consumer considers itself shut down, potentially causing duplicate segment emissions.

findings.title: max_processes defaults to 1 from CLI but None in constructor, creating inconsistent behavior
findings.body: The CLI option `--flusher-processes` has `default=1`, so the factory always receives an integer ≥1 from the CLI. However, `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` declares `flusher_processes: int | None = None`, and `SpanFlusher.__init__` uses `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` — meaning if someone constructs the factory programmatically without passing `flusher_processes` (getting `None`), the flusher spawns one process per shard instead of defaulting to 1. This inconsistency between the CLI default and the programmatic default could surprise callers and should be aligned (e.g., default to 1 in the factory as well).
